definition: DeepDream is a computer vision program created by Google engineer Alexander Mordvintsev that uses a convolutional neural network to find and enhance patterns in images via algorithmic pareidolia, thus creating a dream-like appearance reminiscent of a psychedelic experience in the deliberately overprocessed images.
details: Google's program popularized the term (deep) "dreaming" to refer to the generation of images that produce desired activations in a trained deep network, and the term now refers to a collection of related approaches.

explainer.lead: DeepDream turns the patterns that strongly activate a trained image network into visible, often hallucinatory pictures. It offers a way to inspect what drives responses inside a deep network, and it popularized the idea of neural networks producing “dream” imagery.

tiers.eli5: Imagine staring at clouds until you start seeing faces, then drawing over the clouds to make those faces clearer. DeepDream does something similar with a picture and a computer system that has learned to recognize visual patterns. Repeating this can make an ordinary photo look strange and dreamlike.
tiers.practitioner: Apply it by choosing activations in a trained convolutional neural network and modifying an image so those responses become stronger. Inspect intermediate results and keep the original, because continued enhancement deliberately produces heavily overprocessed textures. The visual result depends on which network responses are selected for enhancement.
tiers.paperLevel: Let A(x) denote selected activations produced by image x in a trained deep network. DeepDream generates or modifies x to produce desired activations, making the associated learned patterns increasingly visible. The process can amplify weak resemblances into algorithmic pareidolia, sacrificing realism for dreamlike imagery; the term now covers a collection of related approaches.

explainer.example: Take a landscape photograph in which a few curved cloud edges weakly resemble a pattern the network responds to. DeepDream strengthens that response and enhances the matching curves; after repetition, the clouds acquire pronounced, unexpected shapes and the whole landscape looks psychedelic rather than photographic.

usedIn.name: Google’s DeepDream program
usedIn.detail: The original computer vision program created by Google engineer Alexander Mordvintsev.

usedIn.name: Deep-network visualization
usedIn.detail: Generating images that produce desired activations helps reveal patterns to which a trained network responds.

usedIn.name: Psychedelic-style image art
usedIn.detail: Deliberate pattern enhancement creates overprocessed pictures with a dreamlike appearance.

explainer.intuition: A trained network already has visual patterns that make parts of it respond strongly. DeepDream works backward from those responses, enhancing matching hints in an image until they become conspicuous, much like deliberately strengthening shapes imagined in clouds.
howItWorks: Start with an image and a trained convolutional neural network.
Choose network activations that the generated image should produce.
Identify patterns in the image associated with those responses.
Modify the image to strengthen the desired activations and their visible patterns.
Repeat until the accumulated enhancements create the characteristic overprocessed, dreamlike appearance.
explainer.whyItMatters: DeepDream made desired network activations visible as imagery, connecting deep-network visualization with a distinctive artistic style. Google’s program also popularized “dreaming” as a term for a broader family of activation-driven image-generation approaches.
misconceptions: It is not simply a decorative photo filter: its changes are driven by activations in a trained deep network.
The network is not literally asleep or dreaming; “dreaming” is a metaphor for activation-driven image generation.
DeepDream is not only the original Google program; the term now includes related approaches.
